title: Owned Trait Objects
goal: Store dynamically sized types on the heap using Box<dyn Trait>.

sections.text: In languages like Java or Python, collections hold objects of different subclasses naturally. In Rust, items in a vector must all have the exact same size at compile time.

sections.caption: Different types implementing Speaker have different sizes.

sections.text: Because types implementing a trait vary in size, you cannot write `Vec<dyn Speaker>` directly. `dyn Speaker` is a dynamically sized type with no fixed size.

sections.caption: Box gives every item a fixed pointer size on the stack.

sections.text: `Box<dyn Speaker>` stores each element on the heap and holds a fat pointer. A fat pointer contains two addresses: one to the heap data, and one to the vtable of methods.
Dynamic dispatch through trait objects adds a small lookup cost at runtime. Generics with trait bounds avoid this cost, and are covered in the Generics vs dyn deck.

explanation: Store dynamically sized types on the heap using Box<dyn Trait>.
